name: Kearney-Thomas

pitch_detail.notes: Crack system continues up the buttress.
Variable rock quality per the original FA account.
Follows crack systems left of a large slot high on the face.
Upper buttress terrain leading toward the crux.
Sustained, well-protected finger crack; the route's technical crux.

descent_text: As with the neighboring Beckey-Tate line, descend by scrambling to the notch just north of the true summit and following the loose scree-and-snow gully back down toward the Hairpin pullout, roughly two hours from the top.
approach: Park at the Hairpin pullout on SR-20 (roughly Milepost 163, about 1 mile east of Washington Pass). Follow the Kangaroo Temple/Wallaby Peak climbers' path south along Early Winters Creek for roughly 2 miles, then leave the trail to cross the creek and ascend the prominent gully system to the base of the south face, taking the left fork at the high Y-junction. Expect 2.5 to 5 hours of approach time; water is unreliable late season.
overview: A longer, harder companion line to Beckey-Tate on the south face's southeast buttress, following crack systems up variable-quality granite to a sustained 5.11a finger-crack crux; one of the more popular technical routes on the peak despite the wall's overall obscurity.
beta: First climbed by Kearney and Thomas up the southeast buttress, following crack systems on the left side of a large slot high on the face over variable rock quality. The line is now graded 5.11a with a well-protected finger-crack crux; it is now listed at 7-8 pitches, reflecting later variation starts (see 'Skinny Start').
fa: Kearney and Thomas (first names and date unknown)
